probe.question: What is the dominant charge state of OC(=O)c1cccnc1 at pH 7.4? It is amphoteric so I do not trust a single pKa here, and I need to know what is actually in solution before I argue about solubility.
forbids_claims: a microstate population the calculation did not return
a predicted pKa presented as the answer to which species dominates
a solubility value, which was not asked for and not computed
probe.direction: The amphoteric case is exactly where the single-site predictor refuses and where the microstate profile earns its cost, and the asker has said so. A good answer enumerates the microstates and ranks them in water at the stated pH, by either route, and reports the dominant form as a structure rather than as a word. The zwitterion question should be addressed explicitly, since single-site toggling does not produce the doubly-ionised form and a reader will assume it was considered. It is a correct and useful answer to add that a single predicted pKa would not have covered this and why. Reaching for the fast pKa predictor and presenting its number as the speciation answer is the failure this probe exists to catch.
